seoTitle: How to Add a Favicon in Hostinger Website Builder (2026)
metaDescription: Add a favicon to your Hostinger site in minutes — open the builder, find General settings, upload a square icon through the media library, and save.
intro: A favicon is the tiny icon that sits in the browser tab beside your site's name, and it is one of the cheapest credibility upgrades a new site can get. On Hostinger's website builder there is no code involved at all — the whole thing is an upload field buried a couple of clicks deep in the builder's settings, which is exactly why people struggle to find it. This guide walks the real path from hostinger.com through hPanel and into the builder, shows what each panel looks like along the way, and covers the file requirements that decide whether your icon renders crisply or turns into a smudge. Budget about five minutes, most of which is making the image rather than uploading it.

steps.heading: Log in to Hostinger and open hPanel
steps.body: Start at hostinger.com and click Log in at the top right of the homepage. The credentials you want are the ones for your Hostinger account itself, not your site's own admin or your domain registrar — a distinction that trips people up when they've bought hosting and a domain in separate places. After signing in you land on hPanel, Hostinger's main control panel, which is the hub for hosting, domains, email, and the website builder. Everything in this guide happens inside the builder, so hPanel is only a waypoint.

steps.heading: Open your site in the website builder
steps.body: From the Home tab in hPanel, find the site you want to change and click Edit Website. That opens the builder in its own workspace: a top bar with device toggles, undo and redo, Connect domain, Preview, and the purple Update website button, plus a narrow icon rail down the left edge. The canvas in the middle is your live page, and clicking any section brings up its own toolbar. None of these on-canvas controls touch the favicon — the icon is a site-wide setting, not part of any one section, so ignore the section toolbars entirely for this task.

image.caption: The Hostinger builder workspace, with the page canvas in the middle and the Update website button waiting at the top right.

steps.heading: Find General settings in the More menu
steps.body: The favicon lives under the three-dot icon at the bottom of the left rail — the More menu. Opening it reveals a long list: Blog, Appointments, General settings, Integrations, Form submissions, Analytics, SEO settings, Media library, Multi-language, Manage backups, and Export content to WordPress. Choose General settings, the third item. It is worth noticing that SEO settings sits in this same menu but is not where the favicon lives, which is the single most common wrong turn — the icon is filed as a general site property, not an SEO field.

image.caption: The More menu open in the left rail, with General settings sitting just above Integrations and well above SEO settings.

steps.heading: Upload the icon from the media library
steps.body: Inside General settings, the Favicon card is the first block on the page. Clicking its image area opens Hostinger's media library, which is shared with the rest of your site — anything already uploaded, like a logo, appears under My library. Use Upload files at the top right to bring in your icon, or pick an existing asset if your logo mark already works at small sizes. The library also offers tabs for AI Images and Free images, but neither is much help here: stock art rarely survives being shrunk to a 16-pixel square. Upload a file you made deliberately for this slot.

image.caption: The media library open over the builder, showing an existing logo in My library and the Upload files button at the top right.

steps.heading: Prepare a file that actually renders well
steps.body: Favicons are displayed at roughly 16x16 or 32x32 pixels, so the artwork has to survive brutal downscaling. Use a square PNG or ICO file, and design for the size rather than reusing a wide horizontal logo — a full wordmark becomes an unreadable grey blur in a tab. If your logo has a distinctive symbol, crop to just that symbol. Keep the contrast high and the detail minimal, and if you use a transparent PNG, check it against both light and dark browser themes, because a dark mark on transparency disappears in a dark tab strip.

image.caption: The Favicon card in General settings after an image is set, with a live browser-tab preview on the right and a Save changes button below.

steps.heading: Save and confirm it went live
steps.body: Click Save changes on the Favicon card and watch for the Saved indicator on the card header. Hostinger shows a small mock browser tab beside the upload area so you can judge the result before publishing, which is the fastest way to catch an icon that is too detailed. Then publish with Update website — a saved builder setting is not the same as a live site, and skipping the publish step is why people insist the favicon 'didn't work'. If the old icon still shows on the live URL afterwards, that is browser caching rather than a failed upload: reload with a hard refresh or open the site in a private window to see the real state.

faq.question: What size and format should a Hostinger favicon be?
faq.answer: A square PNG or ICO file. Browsers render it around 16x16 or 32x32 pixels, so design a simple, high-contrast mark rather than shrinking a full wordmark.

faq.question: Where is the favicon setting in the Hostinger website builder?
faq.answer: Open the three-dot More menu at the bottom of the builder's left rail, choose General settings, and the Favicon card is the first block on that page. It is not under SEO settings, which is the usual wrong turn.

faq.question: Do I need to know any code to add a favicon in Hostinger?
faq.answer: No. The builder handles the HTML link tag for you — you only upload an image and save. Hand-writing a favicon link is only necessary on sites you host yourself.

faq.question: I uploaded the favicon but my site still shows the old one. Why?
faq.answer: Two likely reasons: you saved in the builder but never clicked Update website to publish, or your browser cached the old icon. Publish first, then check the live site in a private window.

faq.question: Does this work on Hostinger's free website builder plan?
faq.answer: Yes. The favicon field is part of General settings in the builder itself, so the process is identical regardless of which builder plan you are on.
